newsitem.title: UK: Stg/mark scales to fresh 4-1/2 yr peak above 2.80.
newsitem.headline: Stg/mark scales to fresh 4-1/2 yr peak above 2.80.

text.p: Sterling scaled to fresh 4-1/2 year peaks after tearing through key psychological resistance at 2.80 marks on Friday, extending its assault on a generally feeble mark in Europe, said analysts.
"People are selling the mark...Sterling/mark is coat-tailing on the back of the mark selling," said Chris Tinker, chief treasury economist at Standard Chartered.
At 1043 GMT sterling was trading at 2.7993/04 marks vs 2.7891/02 marks in late Europe on Thursday, and just off fresh 4-1/2 year peaks of 2.8029 hit on Friday.
Against the dollar, however, sterling was sidelined.
At 1052 GMT sterling was trading at $1.6244, little changed from $1.6222/32 in late Europe on Thursday.
Tinker said if the sterling/mark move had been sterling and not mark related, cable would be much firmer.
"The fact that it hasn't, suggests that we are just seeing a mark correction," said Tinker.

Revived optimism European Monetary Union (EMU) will get off the ground as scheduled has prompted some mark jitters, driving the mark to fresh 45-month lows against the French franc overnight, and new lows against the peseta and escudo, said analysts.
European Union Monetary Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said on Friday he expected economic and monetary union to start on schedule with many countries.
"It is clear that EMU will become reality starting January 1, 1999 and that a significant number of countries will join then," he told a news conference while on a visit to Finland.
"There is no turning back," he said.

Traders said the Bank of England offers for fixed rate round of operations, unchanged at 6.0 percent, implied Chancellor Kenneth Clarke had decided to leave rates unchanged after Thursday's monthly monetary meeting.
"The Bank of England has left rates unchanged, as expected," said a trader at a Belgian bank.
Though its attractiveness as a high-yielding currency, with a its current 10-year yield spread over Germany at 185 basis points the highest in Europe, is clear.
Also in line with forecasts, was a poll on Friday showing the Conservative Party has made only a modest dent in the opposition Labour Party's opinion-poll lead.
A Harris poll commissioned for The Independent newspaper on Friday gave the opposition Labour Party a 22-point lead compared with 24 points the previous week.
With no UK data due on Friday, markets are awaiting U.S. retail sales and producer price figures at 1230 GMT for fresh direction.
The dollar's tone was firm at midday Europe, though trapped in a tight range ahead of the inflation data, said analysts.

"The focus is firmly on the U.S. data...It's all about what the Fed will do in May (at its policy-making meeting) and so all the data out of the U.S. is crucial, especially something like PPI," said Claudio Demolli, foreign exchange analyst at Merrill Lynch.
-- Julia Meehan, London newsroom +44 171 542 6701
